extracted.intended_audience: EPA rule writers, regulatory staff, and Agency standards coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Interim internal guidance and checklist for EPA rule writers to implement the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (NTTAA) and OMB Circular A-119: how to find, evaluate, adopt, document, and participate in voluntary consensus standards when developing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to consider and use VCSs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must consider and use "voluntary consensus standards" (VCS's), if available and applicable, when implementing policies and programs, unless doing so would be "inconsistent with applicable law or otherwise impractical".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NTTAA requirement now; OMB will report annually to Congress when agencies use government-unique standards instead of VCSs and must include explanations. Use the checklist for all rules under development and try to implement the Act's requirements even for rules already proposed or in the pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a "voluntary consensus standard" (VCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A 'voluntary consensus standard' is a technical standard developed or adopted by a legitimate standards-developing organization ('voluntary consensus standards body')." Technical standards are "performance-based or design-specific technical specifications and related management systems practices."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legitimate standards-developing organization must produce standards by consensus and observe the principles of due process, openness, and balance of interests. Examples: ASTM, ISO, IEC, API, NFPA, SAE. ANSI certification (American National Standard designation) is an important indicator of legitimacy. If unsure whether a standard qualifies, seek OGC advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which rules require consideration of VCSs
rubrics_metrics.description: If your rule establishes a technical standard (e.g., a special method for collecting a water sample, field or laboratory procedures for measuring a chemical parameter), it is likely there are existing VCSs you must consider. If a rule does not involve establishment or modification of technical standards, no obligation to address NTTAA in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common potentially-useful VCS types: field/laboratory test methods, sampling protocols, material specifications; possibly quality/environmental management systems, business practices, definitional standards, installation safety codes. Seek out and consider both domestic and international potentially-applicable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find potentially applicable VCSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Search authoritative repositories and services such as the National Standards System Network (NSSN) maintained by ANSI and the National Center for Standards and Certification Information (NIST) telephone/library service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSSN (http://www.nssn.org) provides highlights of >250,000 standards from 600+ bodies; use online keyword searches. Use NIST's phone service for library research. EPA is developing enhanced NSSN services and an internal EPA Standards Network/alert service to make searches easier and to notify staff of relevant activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document NTTAA analysis in rule preambles
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory preambles should summarize the requirements of the NTTAA, describe the Agency's efforts to identify potentially applicable VCSs, identify those standards EPA intends to use in the rule or explain why use would be inconsistent with law or otherwise impractical, and, for proposed rules, solicit public comment on additional VCSs and EPA's analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these sections in preambles routinely; for rules already proposed with closed comment periods, still check standards sources and address any identified standards (consider supplemental notice if appropriate). If EPA decides not to adopt a VCS, explain the rationale in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to issue a supplemental notice or explain non-adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: If you identify a voluntary consensus standard that shows promise for Agency adoption, consider issuing a supplemental notice; alternatively, if you decide not to use the standard, explain your reasons in the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures transparency and complies with NTTAA/OMB expectations. The memorandum explicitly directs rule writers to consider supplemental notices where practicable when new potentially-applicable VCSs are identified after the original proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in voluntary standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should participate in standards development activities of voluntary consensus standards bodies when such participation would be in the public interest and compatible with the Agency's mission, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation furthers Agency goals, facilitates compliance with rulemaking aspects of NTTAA, reduces regulatory cost and burden, and allows the Agency to influence standards outcomes. EPA designates a Standards Executive and Standards Coordinators to manage participation and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and implementation of Performance-Based Measurement System (PBMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: PBMS is defined as a set of processes wherein the data quality needs, mandates or limitations of a program or project are specified and serve as criteria for selecting appropriate methods to meet those needs in a cost-effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where PBMS is implemented, regulated entities may select any appropriate analytical test method to comply with EPA regulations, provided it meets PBMS criteria. PBMS is intended to be consistent with expanded use of VCSs and to reduce problems from incorporating out-of-date specific standards into regulations; EPA anticipates proposing regulatory amendments to incorporate PBMS where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking, alerting, and internal procedures to find standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is developing an internal tracking system, NSSN alert service integration, and written guidelines so rule writers routinely check adherence to NTTAA and can retrieve current information on existing and proposed voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Agency electronic resources and the planned NSSN Alert Service to be notified of standards activity. The interim guidance directs rulewriters to use the attached checklist while comprehensive guidance and systems are developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to report use of government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by P.L. 104-113, agencies must report instances when government-unique standards are used in lieu of voluntary consensus standards, along with explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB will compile and report such decisions annually to Congress. Agencies should document decisions and rationales fully; in the FY1997 examples shown, several agencies reported 'None' for uses of government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and process for judging a standard 'impractical' or inconsistent with law
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule writers must decide whether a potentially-applicable voluntary consensus standard can be used or must be rejected as 'impractical' or 'inconsistent with applicable law'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive guidance (under development) will provide expanded procedures for searching, evaluating, and documenting why a standard is impractical. Until then, consult OGC and your Regulatory Steering Committee Representative and document the decision in the regulatory preamble with the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use checklist for all rules under development (immediate implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program offices are asked to immediately begin using the interim checklist for all rules under development to encourage uniform Agency-wide compliance with NTTAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is interim pending more detailed Agency guidance and revision of OMB Circular A-119; rule writers should rely on the checklist and coordinate with Regulatory Steering Committee reps and OGC for additional help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with OGC and Regulatory Steering Committee Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule writers may seek the advice of OGC in determining whether a standard qualifies as a 'voluntary consensus standard' and in drafting the rationale for adoption or non-adoption; work with Regulatory Steering Committee Representatives for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions arise about standard legitimacy, legal constraints, or drafting preamble language, contact the designated OGC staff attorney on the rule or the program's Regulatory Steering Committee Representative (lists and contacts provided).
